headline: Bats Go Cold At Fenway While A.J. Brown Practice Debut Excites
morning_brew: Fenway was quiet last night as the Sox dropped a tough game to Baltimore, falling four to two. Connelly Early got the start on the mound and took the loss, giving up four runs on six hits over five and a third innings of work. Greg Weissert was a bright spot out of the bullpen with three strikeouts in his relief appearance, but you cannot win games when the bats only produce five hits. Ceddanne Rafaela had a solid night with two hits, but the rest of the lineup just could not spark a rally when we needed it.

This loss drops the club to twenty-five and thirty-four, keeping us anchored at the bottom of the division. We have another matchup with Baltimore tonight at Fenway Park before a massive weekend series in New York against those Yankees. If this team wants to turn things around, the offense has to wake up immediately. It is always a battle against our rivals in the Bronx, and heading down there with cold bats would be an absolute disaster.

Switching over to Foxborough, the excitement is incredibly high after A.J. Brown made his official practice debut in a Patriots uniform. Seeing him out there catching passes from Drake Maye gives you real hope for what this offense can do in the fall. The star receiver looked fantastic on the field, and he already seems to be fitting right in with the team. It is only June, but having a legitimate top-tier weapon on the roster makes the upcoming season feel a whole lot brighter.

news_digest.headline: A.J. Brown makes Patriots practice debut
news_digest.dans_take: Seeing him in New England colors makes the offseason wait feel a whole lot shorter.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox's Garrett Crochet has low-grade lat strain, MRI shows
news_digest.dans_take: Injuries are always tough to see, so hopefully he can recover quickly.

news_digest.dans_take: Computers can project whatever they want, but I only care about what happens on the field.

trend_watch.trend: Early struggled on the mound last night, surrendering four runs over five and a third innings in a four to two loss.
trend_watch.dans_take: He just did not have his best stuff, and we need much more consistency from our starting rotation if we want to climb out of this basement.

trend_watch.trend: Weissert was excellent in relief last night, throwing one and two-thirds perfect innings with three strikeouts.
trend_watch.dans_take: That is exactly what you want to see from a setup guy, as he came in and completely shut down the Baltimore hitters.

trend_watch.trend: Rafaela picked up two of the team's five hits last night while batting out of the outfield.
trend_watch.dans_take: He continues to be a bright spot in this lineup, showing a great approach at the plate right now.
